scope: New versioned analytical protocol; not recovered historical depth definitions, a scientific completion claim, or a prediction accuracy claim.

levels.title: Application and review-cycle identity
levels.objective: Resolve the exact drug, indication, formulation, application and review cycle before comparing evidence.
requirements: Bind application, indication, formulation and review cycle to primary regulatory records.
Keep delays, withdrawals, complete responses and approvals distinct; do not infer a decision from a target date.
completion_artifacts: Primary application/cycle identity record with unresolved aliases documented.

levels.title: Point-in-time evidence boundary
levels.objective: Separate the research cutoff, source availability, retrospective review and original prediction freeze.
requirements: Document the original prediction cutoff or explicitly preserve it as unknown.
Establish public availability before the research cutoff; an action date, printed date or folder year is insufficient.
Keep retrospective review timestamps separate from source publication and original prediction generation.
completion_artifacts: Timestamped source-availability ledger and explicit cutoff/freezing chronology.

levels.title: Source corpus and reconciliation
levels.objective: Collect and reconcile original documents, corrections and contradictory disclosures without promoting leads.
requirements: Retain original source bytes and hashes, accession identities and relevant locations.
Identify corrected, superseded, duplicated and unavailable documents and reconcile conflicting claims.
Exclude outcome-only and post-cutoff material from pre-decision findings.
completion_artifacts: Versioned source inventory, byte/hash provenance and exclusion/reconciliation log.

levels.title: Mechanistic and translational context
levels.objective: Assess biological rationale and translation to the proposed indication without assuming mechanism implies efficacy.
requirements: Document mechanism, target engagement, translational limitations and pathway-relevant evidence.
Distinguish direct clinical evidence from extrapolation across diseases, formulations or treatment settings.
completion_artifacts: Source-bound mechanistic rationale with contrary findings and translational limitations.

levels.title: Population and comparator suitability
levels.objective: Assess eligibility, selection and comparator relevance to the intended use.
requirements: Verify trial inclusion/exclusion, baseline characteristics and analysis-population denominators.
Justify concurrent comparator choice and identify selection or enrichment limitations.
completion_artifacts: Protocol-linked population/comparator assessment and denominator reconciliation.

levels.title: Design and protocol integrity
levels.objective: Evaluate randomization, blinding, amendments and deviations as potential sources of bias.
requirements: Review protocol versions, allocation methods, blinding, deviations and amendment timing.
Identify changes made after relevant data access and their consequences.
completion_artifacts: Dated protocol/amendment history and design-bias review.

levels.title: Power and prespecified analysis
levels.objective: Establish the power assumptions and statistical analysis plan frozen before relevant data review.
requirements: Verify sample-size assumptions, event targets and plausible treatment effects.
Retain the dated statistical plan and document changes relative to data access.
completion_artifacts: Prespecification and power assessment with dated protocol/SAP support.

levels.title: Primary efficacy and clinical meaning
levels.objective: Evaluate the primary treatment effect and uncertainty against clinically relevant thresholds.
requirements: Verify primary endpoint definition, analysis population, effect estimate, uncertainty and statistical assumptions.
Distinguish statistical significance, effect magnitude and clinical relevance.
completion_artifacts: Reproducible primary endpoint/effect-size assessment with uncertainty and clinical interpretation.

levels.title: Secondary endpoints and multiplicity
levels.objective: Evaluate secondary findings under the actual type-I-error strategy.
requirements: Reconstruct endpoint hierarchy, multiplicity control and failed gates.
Separate confirmatory secondary outcomes from nominal or exploratory findings.
completion_artifacts: Endpoint hierarchy and multiplicity assessment linked to prespecified tests.

levels.title: Estimands and missing data
levels.objective: Evaluate the treatment question, intercurrent events, exclusions and missing-data assumptions.
requirements: Reconcile randomized, treated, evaluable and reported analysis populations.
Assess estimand, intercurrent-event strategy, missingness assumptions and informative dropout.
completion_artifacts: Estimand/denominator reconciliation with missing-data bias assessment.

levels.title: Sensitivity, subgroup and durability
levels.objective: Challenge robustness across analyses, populations and time.
requirements: Review prespecified sensitivity analyses, subgroup interaction evidence and follow-up.
Separate within-arm change from between-arm effects and subgroup observations from proven heterogeneity.
completion_artifacts: Robustness assessment with subgroup, sensitivity and durability limitations.

levels.title: Serious harms and discontinuations
levels.objective: Characterize serious adverse events, deaths and discontinuations with correct denominators and context.
requirements: Reconcile adverse-event definitions, seriousness, causality, severity and discontinuation denominators.
Review deaths and withdrawals in both arms rather than relying on selected tolerability summaries.
completion_artifacts: Safety event/denominator assessment with causality and competing explanations.

levels.title: Organ toxicity and exposure safety
levels.objective: Assess organ-specific risks and adequacy of exposure for the proposed use.
requirements: Review laboratory, organ-specific and class risks, exposure duration and at-risk populations.
Identify limits of long-term or repeated-use safety and restrictions on exposure.
completion_artifacts: Exposure-adjusted safety and organ-risk assessment with missing long-term requirements.

levels.title: Benefit-risk and generalizability
levels.objective: Integrate benefit and harm for the intended clinical setting without converting gaps into a directional conclusion.
requirements: Compare benefits and harms at matched exposure and in the intended population.
Assess transferability to clinical practice, unmet need and uncertainty; missing evidence stays unknown.
completion_artifacts: Population-specific benefit-risk analysis with explicit uncertainties and competing interpretations.

levels.title: Consistency and independent reproducibility
levels.objective: Compare all relevant studies and reconcile registry, publications and sponsor disclosures.
requirements: Identify supportive and failed studies within the program and distinguish independent replication from reuse.
Reconcile registered, published and disclosed analyses and verify principal calculations where possible.
completion_artifacts: Cross-study reconciliation and independent verification record with unresolved conflicts.

levels.title: Regulatory pathway and interactions
levels.objective: Verify pathway-specific evidence requirements, FDA interactions and special designations.
requirements: Establish application pathway, relevant FDA feedback and endpoint agreements from actual records.
Verify special designations and their scope without treating them as approval or relaxed safety standards.
completion_artifacts: Pathway/interaction/designation matrix with source-supported implications and unknowns.

levels.title: Manufacturing process and product quality
levels.objective: Assess process characterization, scale readiness, analytical methods and stability.
requirements: Identify formulation, critical quality attributes, process controls, validation and commercial-scale evidence.
Review specifications, analytical methods and stability; do not equate sponsor assertions with an FDA inspection.
completion_artifacts: CMC process/quality assessment tied to the exact product and manufacturing version.

levels.title: Facilities, deficiencies and supply risk
levels.objective: Investigate inspection readiness, quality systems and unresolved manufacturing or supply deficiencies.
requirements: Bind facilities, inspections, vendors and deficiencies to the exact review cycle and evidence cutoff.
Assess corrective actions, quality-system readiness and supply-chain risks, including opposing evidence.
completion_artifacts: Facility/deficiency/corrective-action ledger with cutoff-bound uncertainty.

levels.title: Historical comparisons and standard of care
levels.objective: Select historical clinical and regulatory comparators without outcome-based selection or duplicated cycles.
requirements: Prespecify comparator selection and account for indication, mechanism, population, design, endpoints, treatment era and CMC differences.
Verify action-cycle identities, denominator completeness and program-family independence before model use.
Distinguish clinical context and within-program studies from independent FDA decision precedents.
completion_artifacts: Source-linked comparator matrix, exclusions and family/cycle deduplication proof.

levels.title: Adversarial synthesis and frozen handoff
levels.objective: Challenge the strongest opposing decision and assemble an independently reviewed dossier with a reproducible handoff.
requirements: Test the strongest clinical, statistical, safety, manufacturing and regulatory case for the opposite decision.
Record unresolved evidence, reviewer disagreement and conditions requiring abstention.
Bind the reviewed evidence version and model/prediction chronology separately; this scientific protocol does not establish forecasting accuracy.
completion_artifacts: Independent adversarial review, unresolved-requirement ledger and versioned evidence handoff; no prediction validation inferred.
